indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B3.2.2.1: Demonstrate understanding of life cycle of a plant
indicator.objective: Observe the germination of maize and bean seeds

skills.description: Understand that germination is the process of a seed sprouting and beginning to grow into a new plant
Identify the conditions seeds need to germinate (water/moisture, air, warmth)
Compare seeds in wet conditions vs. dry conditions to see which germinate
Describe the steps of setting up the germination experiment
Record or predict what happens to the seeds over time

misconceptions: Dry seeds are dead and can never grow.
All seeds sprout at the same time.
A seed turns into a fully grown plant immediately after sprouting.

questions.stem: What is the process called when a seed begins to sprout and grow?
hints: It happens when a seed comes to life.
questions.explanation: Germination is the process where a seed sprouts and begins to grow into a new plant.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse plant growth processes with physical changes of matter.

questions.stem: What do seeds need to germinate?
questions.explanation: Seeds need water, air, and warmth to germinate. Sunlight is not required initially.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think seeds only need soil and sunlight.

questions.stem: If you put a bean seed in wet cotton wool and another in dry cotton wool, which one will sprout?
options: The one in wet cotton wool
The one in dry cotton wool
hints: Dry cotton wool has no water.
questions.explanation: The seed in wet cotton wool will sprout because it has the moisture it needs to germinate.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think seeds can sprout without water.

questions.stem: What will you first observe when a bean seed starts to germinate?
options: The seed turning into a stone
questions.explanation: The first visible sign of germination is usually the tiny root emerging from the seed.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a full leaf appears first.

questions.stem: In the germination experiment, what is the cotton wool used for?
options: To hold water and keep the seed moist
To make the seed grow faster
questions.explanation: The cotton wool acts as a bed that holds water and keeps the seed moist.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the cotton wool is food for the seed.

questions.stem: Why do we keep the cotton wool moist (damp) and not completely flooded with water?
options: Seeds need air, and too much water might block the air
Seeds can only drink a little water
Flooding makes the seeds too cold
The water will wash the seed away
hints: Too much water drowns the seed.
questions.explanation: Seeds need air to germinate. If the cotton wool is flooded, it blocks the air from reaching the seed.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think more water is always better.

questions.stem: After one week, the seed in the dry container has not sprouted. Why?
hints: What was missing from the dry cotton wool?
questions.explanation: Without water, the seed cannot begin the germination process.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the lack of soil is the problem.

questions.stem: After the tiny root appears, what grows next from the seed?
questions.explanation: After the root emerges, the shoot (stem and small leaves) grows upwards towards the light.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a mature fruit appears next.

questions.stem: When setting up the experiment, where should you place the seeds in the container?
options: Between the cotton wool and the side of the glass
At the very bottom under all the cotton wool
Floating on top of the water
hints: You want to see them clearly.
questions.explanation: Placing the seeds against the side of the glass allows you to observe them clearly as they germinate.
questions.misconception: Pupils may bury the seeds too deep to see.

questions.stem: Do seeds need sunlight to begin germinating in the cotton wool experiment?
options: No, they can germinate in the dark
Yes, they must be in direct sunlight
Yes, but only for one hour a day
hints: Think about seeds buried in soil.
They sprout before reaching the surface.
questions.explanation: Most seeds do not need sunlight to germinate. They need water, air, and warmth. They only need light after the leaves appear.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think seeds need sunlight to sprout.

questions.stem: What is the name of the process when a seed sprouts?
questions.explanation: The process is called germination.

questions.stem: Name two things a seed needs to germinate.
questions.explanation: Seeds need water and air (and warmth) to germinate.
questions.misconception: Pupils may say soil or sunlight.

questions.stem: Ama sets up her germination experiment but forgets to add water to the cotton wool. What will happen?
options: The seeds will grow into huge plants
The seeds will turn into soil
hints: Water is a basic need for germination.
questions.explanation: Without water, the seeds cannot germinate and will remain dormant or dry up.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think seeds can grow without water.

questions.stem: Why did the seeds in the cotton wool without soil still germinate?
options: Because seeds only need water, air, and warmth at this stage; soil is not necessary for germination
Because cotton wool is a type of soil
Because soil is not needed by plants at all
hints: What did the cotton wool provide?
Do seeds need soil to sprout?
questions.explanation: Seeds carry their own food for the initial stage. They only need water, air, and warmth to germinate, which the cotton wool provided.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think soil is absolutely required from day one.

questions.stem: You set up two containers: Container A has seeds in wet cotton wool, and Container B has seeds in dry cotton wool. After one week, describe what you will see in each container.

criteria.description: States Container A will have sprouted seeds (roots/shoots)
States Container B will have unsprouted/dry seeds

hints: What happens to a dry seed?
questions.explanation: Container A will show germination because it has water. Container B will show no germination because it lacks water.

questions.stem: Describe what a bean seed looks like 5 days after it has been placed in wet cotton wool.

criteria.description: Mentions the seed coat has split open
Mentions a small root and/or a tiny green shoot has appeared

hints: Does the outer skin stay whole?
questions.explanation: After 5 days, the seed coat should be split, and a small white root and a tiny green shoot should be visible.

questions.stem: Show your teacher how to set up a germination experiment for a maize seed using a transparent container and cotton wool.

criteria.description: Places cotton wool in the container
Puts the seed between the cotton wool and the glass
Adds a little water to moisten the cotton wool

hints: Make sure you can see the seed.
Do not flood it with water.
questions.explanation: This tests the practical steps of setting up the experiment.

questions.stem: In your experiment, the roots grow downwards into the cotton wool, and the shoot grows upwards. Why does the shoot grow upwards?
options: To reach the light it needs for making food later
Because the seed wants to escape
hints: What does a green plant need?
questions.explanation: After germination, the shoot grows upwards towards the light so the plant can make its own food.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think roots and shoots grow randomly.

questions.stem: A farmer plants maize seeds but the weather is very cold and there is no rain. What will likely happen to the seeds?
options: They will not germinate because they lack water and warmth
They will germinate in one hour
hints: Cold and dry conditions are not good for sprouting.
questions.explanation: Without water and sufficient warmth, the maize seeds will remain dormant and not germinate.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think seeds germinate in any weather.

questions.stem: Tell your teacher what you observed happening to your seed over the week.

criteria.description: States that the seed swelled up/split open
States that a root emerged and then a small shoot

questions.explanation: This tests the ability to accurately describe observations of germination.
